repo.description:
> [!NOTE]
> **Fixed in Logto 1.46.0** (https://github.com/logto-io/logto/pull/9849). Upgrade to 1.46.0 or later. The fix is in Logto core, so connectors don't need updating.

---

I am the author of logto-io/logto#9849 (sanitizing `got` errors in the core error handler). While addressing a review comment on that PR, I found a related issue that goes beyond logging, so I am reporting it privately through this advisory.

## Summary

When an outbound request made by a connector fails at the network level (timeout, connection reset, DNS failure), several connectors wrap the raw `got` `RequestError` in a `ConnectorError`:

- `packages/connectors/connector-sendgrid-email/src/index.ts` (`throw new ConnectorError(ConnectorErrorCodes.General, error)`)
- `connector-mailgun`, `connector-http-email`, `connector-smtp2go-email`, `connector-saml` do the same.

A `got` `RequestError` carries the full request `Options` as an enumerable property, and `Options.toJSON()` returns its internals: headers (including `Authorization: Bearer <SendGrid API key>`), `username`/`password` (Mailgun basic auth, also embedded in the serialized `url` as `https://api:<key>@api.mailgun.net/...`), `json`/`form` bodies (recipient address, verification code).

Two sinks then expose that object:

1. **HTTP response body.** `packages/core/src/middleware/koa-connector-error-handler.ts` converts the `ConnectorError` into `new RequestError({ code: 'connector.general', status: 400, errorDescription: JSON.stringify(data) }, data)`. `RequestError.toBody()` (`packages/core/src/errors/RequestError/index.ts`) returns `pick(this, 'code', 'data', 'details')`, so `data` - the serialized `got` error with the credentials - is sent to the caller. The `errorDescription` interpolation also puts the same JSON in the i18n `message`.
2. **Audit logs.** `packages/core/src/middleware/koa-audit-log.ts` stores `pick(error, 'message', 'code', 'data')` in the `logs` table, which is readable in the Console and through the Management API.

The endpoints that send a verification code (`POST /api/verification-codes`, the experience API `.../verifications/verification-code`, `routes-me/verification-code`) are reachable without authentication, so an anonymous caller who requests a code during a provider outage receives the provider API key in a 400 response.

## Reproduction (reasoning, verified at the unit level)

```js
import { RequestError, Options } from 'got';
import { ConnectorError, ConnectorErrorCodes } from '@logto/connector-kit';

const options = new Options('https://api.sendgrid.com/v3/mail/send', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer SG.FAKE' },
  json: { from: 'a@b.c' },
});
const gotError = new RequestError('Timeout awaiting request', { code: 'ETIMEDOUT' }, options);
const wrapped = new ConnectorError(ConnectorErrorCodes.General, gotError);

wrapped.message.includes('SG.FAKE');                       // true
JSON.stringify({ data: wrapped.data }).includes('SG.FAKE'); // true - what toBody() returns
```

End to end: configure the SendGrid connector, make `api.sendgrid.com` unreachable (hosts file or egress rule), then `POST /api/verification-codes` with an email address. The 400 body contains `data.options.headers.authorization`.

## Suggested fix

Never let a raw `got` error become `data`. Either:

- in `@logto/connector-kit`, make `ConnectorError` reduce an `Error` passed as `data` to `{ name, code, message }` (drop `options`, `request`, `response`), which fixes every connector at once; or
- in `koa-connector-error-handler.ts`, sanitize `data` before building the `RequestError` (the `sanitizeError` helper from #9849 can be reused), and never interpolate the raw JSON into `errorDescription`;
- and in the email/SMS connectors, pass `error.message` rather than the error object (as `connector-vonage-sms` already does).

## Impact note

Self-hosted deployments that use the SendGrid, Mailgun, SMTP2GO or HTTP email connectors are affected on every network-level failure towards the provider. HTTP errors (4xx/5xx from the provider) take a different branch in those connectors and are not affected.
repo.summary: Email/SMS connector credentials returned in the API response body and stored in audit logs on an outbound network error
